spans.text: B is not a leak. It is one crash taking the person's authority away and never giving it back. C is the one you called nastier than a leak, and it is: the host and the world disagreeing about who is in the world.
1 · The law, and where it is enforced
A channel is either committed to one live connection, or rolled back completely. There is no timed-out-but-still-starting state.
Bridge owns capabilities; Connection executes them.
It is what the code already did, and it is the right shape for what Super is becoming — worlds and authority above transient engine processes rather than inside them.
